answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the pearl schedule in the canyon ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the zephyr checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 208 aliases thus means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. That is 34 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
